title: Union transfer waiting periods
summary: Durham explains the six-month wait for new members in New York, how transfers work now, and his membership in four locals at once.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Well, now, when you leave him to go to Lunceford, how did that come about?
Well, you see, after the union was bothering me so much, I didn't like to be antagonized, waiting around like that, and then I just -- I went to a band where I could play.
Well, now, when you came into a city like New York, how long did you have to sit around before you could --
Six months.
Well, how did they think you lived?
Let's see, now, how did you do that? You'd have to sweat it out some kind of way.
Well, when did they change that?
Quite a while -- quite a few years back.
What do you have to do now?
You have to put in an application, and you sign up and go on the application as a traveling member.
Yeah.

And if you was in the city, you had to go out and play dates out until you became a member, but you had to let them know when you went out and came back. You'd live in the city and go get your gig somewhere else.
So you could -- but once you'd done that, you could be, like, a member of a Chicago local and New York, could you?

Yeah, you could stay with both locals if you wanted to, but you had two dues to pay. I did it, I belonged to four unions at one time for a long time. To 627 in Kansas City, 710, Washington, D. C., I was on the board of directors there, at the same time I belonged to New York City and I belonged to the union in Connecticut.
Well, what is the position today? I'm never quite clear about that. I mean, if you're a member --
I don't think you put transfers in there.
If you're a member of the union, you're a member of the union.
Yeah, you just pay white dues. Like up here where we are, I pay $60 a month.
But that's the local.
Yeah.
I got you.
Yeah, setting half of the scale, I think.
Yeah.
Yeah.
